hints: Sorting answers this, but it costs O(n log n). What question would you have to ask about a number to grow a run without sorting?
Membership: given v, is v + 1 also present? A set answers that in constant time.
Only start counting from a number that begins a run - one where v - 1 is absent. Every run then gets walked exactly once.

Put the values in a set. For each value v with v - 1 not in the set, walk v + 1, v + 2 and so on while they are present, and record the length. The inner walk is bounded by the total number of distinct values, so the whole thing stays linear.
